tags.name: Gorgonia Valley
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15 (4 independent domains). Removed 'eagle rays' claim -- no source confirms eagle rays at this specific site (likely confused with Boulari Pass or a generic regional list); this was a hallucination surviving the prior QA pass. Added pygmy seahorses, confirmed by newcaledonia.travel and justgottadive.com ('Beyond the Garden of Eden'). Depth conflict: McFadyen reports the wall running 10m to 35m+; justgottadive.com's separate trip report gives a maximum of 50m for the same site. Both figures now noted in the markdown rather than picking one.

tags.name: Oupere Grotto
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: of the 3 previously-listed sources, only michaelmcfadyenscuba.info (page_id=498) actually names and describes Oupere Grotto -- newcaledonia.travel's diving page does not mention it by name (it describes a separate 'Gadji Cave' entry that cannot be confirmed as the same site), and newcaledonia.co.nz (things-to-do-in-isle-of-pines) now 404s. Removed both from validation_source rather than pad the count. Per instructions, validated left as-is since the underlying McFadyen description (caves/tunnels/arches, 5m reef top descending beyond 30m) is unchanged and credible, but this site does NOT currently meet the 3-independent-domain bar -- flagged as unresolved. Left as a candidate for further dive-shop research.

tags.name: Devils Grotto
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: newcaledonia.co.nz (previously cited) now 404s; replaced with sudtourisme.nc, which independently confirms freshwater, the Kere-tribe/airfield-road location, and the N2/50-dive minimum for the Kunie Scuba Centre cave dive. 3 independent domains (newcaledonia.travel, justgottadive.com, sudtourisme.nc) now all agree the pool is freshwater and max depth is 6m, reconfirming the prior QA's rejection of McFadyen's lone 'nominally fresh (actually saline)' claim.

tags.name: Boulari Pass
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: depth is genuinely disputed across all 3 independent sources -- newcaledonia-diving.com states avg 18m/max 26m; McFadyen's dive log describes dropping to 21m on the reef side and rising to ~15m in the pass itself; scubadiverlife.com states avg 15m (49ft)/max 30m (98ft). All three figures now noted in the markdown instead of picking one. Manta ray reputation strongly reconfirmed (McFadyen: 7 mantas in one dive incl. a formation of 5; newcaledonia-diving.com and scubadiverlife.com both confirm mantas as the headline draw). Shark-feeding ban (2012) reconfirmed via newcaledonia-diving.com and a secondary web search on New Caledonia's 2012 shark-feeding/fishing ban; McFadyen's own feeding-demonstration account predates the ban and is now framed as a historical account, not current practice.

tags.name: La Dieppoise
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: added plongee-infos.com (French wreck-history source) as a 4th independent domain. New conflicts surfaced on cross-check: length reported as 46m (Wikipedia, McFadyen) vs 50m (plongee-infos.com); displacement reported as 390 long tons (Wikipedia, McFadyen) vs 370 tonnes (plongee-infos.com); pennant number given as P655 (McFadyen, plongee-infos.com) vs P665 (newcaledonia-diving.com, likely a typo). Both length and tonnage ranges now written into the markdown as sourced disagreements rather than a single picked figure, per wreck-history policy. Build/launch date (laid down 8 Jun 1951, launched 21 Jun 1952), scuttling date (19 Jan 1988, delayed from 12 Jan by Cyclone Anne, via controlled explosives at bow/stern) and vessel identity (ex-HMCS Chaleur, MCB 144) remain confirmed across all 4 sources. Wreck condition softened from 'remarkably intact' to reflect that newcaledonia-diving.com and plongee-infos.com both describe significant wooden-hull deterioration that has opened up the interior compartments, rather than an intact structure. Zentacle.com listing found during research (sinking date '7/08/1996', depth 65.6ft) contradicts every other source and was excluded as unreliable, not cited.

tags.name: False Pass
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: located and confirmed the specific McFadyen page for this site (page_id=508, titled 'False Pass - Noumea, New Caledonia', plus a matching narrative passage on page_id=509 captioned 'A magnificent gorgonia at False Pass' describing the 25m tunnel exiting at 32m, turtle/tuna/trevally/grouper encounter). This is genuinely 2 corroborating passages but both are on the same domain. Extensively searched for independent confirmation (ScubaBoard, Poum/Malabou operator sites, worldadventuredivers.com, farandawayadventures.com, thescubanews.com, newcaledonia.travel Poum/Koumac guide, scubago.com) -- none contain site-specific False Pass content; newcaledonia.travel and scubago.com were removed from validation_source as they do not actually name or describe this site. A ScubaBoard-derived 'Fausse Passe' description (3-12m, sandy plateau) was also found but could not be geolocated to this Poum-area site and was not used -- it likely refers to a different, similarly-named pass elsewhere in the lagoon. Per instructions, validated left as-is since content is unchanged and credible, but flagged as unresolved for the 3-independent-domain bar.

tags.name: Les Pitons
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15 -- SIGNIFICANT FINDING: on McFadyen's own site, 'Les Pitons' is only a bare, empty navigation heading (page_id=509) with no accompanying description; the caves/tunnels/holes/bays/'totally surrounded by reef' description previously published under this site name is verbatim from McFadyen's page literally titled 'False Pass - Noumea, New Caledonia' (page_id=508). No independent source (searched newcaledonia.travel, scubago.com, worldadventuredivers.com, farandawayadventures.com) names a distinct 'Les Pitons' dive site at all. This may not be a genuine standalone site separate from False Pass, or may simply be undocumented online. Prior QA (2026-06-18) had already flagged type uncertainty here; this pass adds identity uncertainty on top. Markdown rewritten to disclose this explicitly. Per instructions, validated left as-is pending resolution, but flagged as unresolved -- recommend either merging/removing this entry or sourcing it directly from a Poum-area dive operator (Pacific Diving / Malabou Beach Resort) in a future pass.

tags.name: Amadee Island Reef
tags.qa_note: Re-audit 2026-08-15: replaced the homepage-only michaelmcfadyenscuba.info citation (no specific Amadee page could be located on his site) with freestyletraveling.com, which independently confirms the sea snake population and turtle sightings at Amadee specifically. 3 independent domains now: newcaledonia.travel (amedee-lighthouse), snorkeling-report.com, freestyletraveling.com. Removed 'parrotfish' from marine life -- not confirmed by any source found for this specific site (snorkeling-report.com's confirmed list is triggerfish, angelfish, clownfish, butterflyfish, wrasses, groupers, trevally, porcupinefish, razorfish, occasional whitetip reef sharks, dugongs). A solopassport.com trip report describing manta rays and a grey nurse shark on an 'Amedee' dive was found but excluded -- those species read as a Boulari Pass encounter bundled into the same boat trip, not confirmed as occurring on the shallow reef immediately around the island.
